examples.en: I have had a rival since school.
Those two are eternal rivals.
Thanks to my rival, I studied harder.
I practice every day to beat my rival.
We ended the match by shaking hands with my rival.

examples.ko: 라이벌은 적이 아니라 힘이 되는 사람이에요.
examples.en: A rival is not an enemy but someone who gives you strength.

explain: '경쟁자'는 일반적인 말이고, '라이벌'은 실력이 비슷해서 서로 의식하는 상대에게 써요. 사이가 나쁘다는 뜻은 아니에요.

phrases.en: We became rivals at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 의식하는 상대가 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means two people became opponents who keep an eye on each other.

phrases.en: Our team played against our rival team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이 비슷한 상대 팀을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an opposing team of similar strength.

phrases.en: That person is my competitor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '라이벌'보다 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general word than 라이벌.

explain_en: 'Gyeongjaengja' (competitor) is the general word; 'raibeol' is for an opponent of similar skill whom you keep an eye on. It does not mean the relationship is bad.

examples.en: The youngest daughter looks the most like her father.

examples.ko: 막내딸 덕분에 우리 집은 늘 웃음이 끊이지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to our youngest daughter, our house is always full of laughter.
Our youngest daughter became a college student this year.
I sent a little pocket money to my youngest daughter.
I went to the market with my youngest daughter.
I prepared a birthday cake for my youngest daughter.

explain: 딸 중에서 가장 어린 딸이에요. 반대로 첫째 딸은 '맏딸'이라고 해요. 집에서 부를 때는 이름 대신 '막내야'라고 부르는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.example: 저는 막내딸이라서 언니들이 잘 챙겨 줘요.
phrases.en: Since I'm the youngest daughter, my older sisters look after me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이라서'를 붙여 막내딸이어서 생기는 일의 이유를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -이라서 gives being the youngest daughter as a reason.

phrases.en: I was born the youngest daughter of three children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기소개에서 가족 중 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in self-introductions to say your place in the family.

phrases.en: Our youngest daughter sings well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우리'를 붙여 가족을 다정하게 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 우리 is a warm way to talk about your own family.

explain_en: It means the youngest of the daughters. The opposite, the eldest daughter, is '맏딸'. At home people often call her '막내야' instead of using her name.

examples.ko: 배달원이 문 앞에 음식을 놓고 갔어요.
examples.en: The delivery person left the food at the door.
I thanked the delivery person.

examples.ko: 배달원은 비 오는 날에도 바쁘게 일해요.
examples.en: Delivery workers work busily even on rainy days.

examples.ko: 우리 집 근처 치킨집은 배달원을 구해요.
examples.en: The chicken restaurant near my house is looking for a delivery worker.

examples.ko: 배달원 아저씨가 길을 잘 몰라서 전화하셨어요.
examples.en: The delivery man did not know the way and called.
Delivery riders on motorcycles pass along the street.

explain: 음식 배달을 하는 사람은 '배달원', 택배를 나르는 사람은 '택배 기사'라고 불러요. 직접 부를 때는 '배달 기사님'이라고 높여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Thank you, delivery driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 말할 때 높여서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form used when addressing or talking about the person.

phrases.en: A motorcycle delivery person is crossing the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 배달하는지 앞에 붙여서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can add how they deliver before the word.

phrases.en: The delivery person will arrive soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배달이 도착하는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the delivery is arriving.

explain_en: A person who delivers food is a '배달원', and a person who carries parcels is a '택배 기사'. When speaking to them, people sometimes say '배달 기사님' to show respect.

examples.en: My husband's younger brother is getting married next month.
I work at the same company as my husband's younger brother.
I gave my husband's younger brother a little pocket money.
My husband's younger brother and his wife came to greet us on the holiday.
My husband's younger brother cooks well, so I often eat his food.
My husband's younger brother is three years younger than me.

explain: 남편의 남동생을 가리켜요. 남편의 여동생은 '시누이'예요. 직접 부를 때는 미혼이면 '도련님', 결혼했으면 '서방님'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 막내 시동생이 다음 달에 군대에 가요.
phrases.en: My youngest brother-in-law goes into the army next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시동생이 여러 명일 때 막내를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the youngest when there are several.

phrases.en: I sent a gift to my husband's brother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '네'를 붙이면 그 사람의 집이나 가족을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 네 means that person's home or family.

phrases.en: I got a call from my husband's younger brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '한테'를 붙여 사람에게 받거나 주는 말을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle 한테 is used for giving to or getting from a person.
phrases.en_equiv: from or to the husband's younger brother

explain_en: It means the husband's younger brother, while the husband's younger sister is a '시누이'. You address him as '도련님' if he is unmarried and '서방님' if he is married.

examples.en: Applicants must write their name and the date.
There were too many applicants, so we decided by lottery.
Please check the applicants for this lecture.
I sent a text message to the applicants.
We give a small gift to applicants.
We chose three people from among the applicants.

explain: '-자'가 붙어 사람을 나타내요. 신청한 사람은 '신청자', 참가하는 사람은 '참가자', 지원하는 사람은 '지원자'예요. 신청하는 일은 '신청하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I applied for a Korean class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청자가 하는 행동을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what an applicant does.

phrases.en: My name is on the applicant list.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청한 사람들의 이름을 적은 목록이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A list of the names of people who applied.

phrases.en: Submit the application form and wait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청할 때 쓰는 종이나 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The paper or form used when applying.

explain_en: The ending '-자' marks a person: '신청자' applied, '참가자' participates, and '지원자' volunteers or applies for a job. The action is '신청하다'.

examples.en: That actress acts really well.
I wanted to become an actress since I was little.
I met a famous actress at the film festival.

examples.ko: 새 영화의 주인공은 신인 여배우로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: A newcomer actress was chosen as the lead of the new movie.
I read that actress's interview in a magazine.
I want to take a photo with that actress.

explain: 여배우는 여자 배우를 가리켜요. 요즘은 성별 없이 그냥 '배우'라고 하는 경우도 많아요. 반대로 남자 배우는 '남자 배우'라고 풀어서 말할 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: Do you know that actress?
phrases.nuance_ko: '여배우'를 풀어서 말한 것이고, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of '여배우', with the same meaning.

phrases.en: She is a popular actress these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기가 많은 여배우를 말할 때 앞에 '인기'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '인기' before it for a popular actress.

phrases.en: I saw a famous actress on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'이 뒤의 '여배우'를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '유명한' describes the noun '여배우' after it.

explain_en: 여배우 means a female actor. Nowadays many people just say '배우' without mentioning gender. For male actors people often say it in two words, '남자 배우'.

examples.en: I am the second son among three brothers.
The second son is much taller than his older brother.
The neighbors' second son is getting married this fall.

examples.ko: 차남인 저는 형과 성격이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: As the second son, my personality is very different from my brother's.
I was introduced to the boss's second son.
My parents gave the second son the same allowance too.

explain: 아들의 순서는 '장남, 차남, 삼남'이라고 해요. 딸은 '장녀, 차녀, 삼녀'예요. 가장 어린 아들은 '막내아들'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I am my parents' second son.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차남'과 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '차남' and easier in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I'm the second child in my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아들이나 딸 모두에게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for both a son and a daughter.

phrases.en: The eldest son and the second son work together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형제의 순서를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to mention the order of brothers together.

explain_en: Sons are ranked '장남, 차남, 삼남', and daughters '장녀, 차녀, 삼녀'. The youngest son can also be called '막내아들'.

examples.en: The Korean people eat tteokguk on Lunar New Year.
Koreans living abroad also learn Hangeul.
I'm studying the history of the Korean people.
If you're Korean, everyone knows this song.
I tried a traditional Korean game.
The Korean people have eaten rice for a long time.

explain: '한국 사람'은 지금 한국에 사는 사람을 떠올리기 쉽지만, '한민족'은 같은 민족이라는 점을 강조해서 해외에 사는 사람까지 함께 말할 때 써요. 뉴스, 역사, 행사 이름에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 우리 한민족은 오랜 역사를 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: We, the Korean people, have a long history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 민족이라는 마음을 강조할 때 앞에 '우리'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 우리 emphasizes a sense of shared people.

phrases.en: Seollal is a holiday of the Korean people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화나 전통을 설명할 때 '한민족의 ~'로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as '한민족의 ~' when explaining culture or tradition.

phrases.en: We are all of the Korean people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 민족임을 말할 때 서술어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate to say we belong to the same people.

explain_en: '한국 사람' tends to suggest people living in Korea now, but '한민족' stresses a shared ethnic identity and can include Koreans living overseas too. It often appears in news, history and event titles.
